verdicts.reason: Foundry eMRAM is real and open to fabless designers: GF AutoPro150 on 22FDX (Dresden, PDK self-serve), TSMC 22ULL eMRAM and 22RRAM. R1 passes, and the T2 path is far below $1B. But 'weights and working data' in eMRAM is wrong. At the card's ~5e5-cycle endurance, working data and activations must stay in on-die SRAM, so the eMRAM holds weights and code only. The space is already occupied. Renesas RA8P1 ships up to 1MB of eMRAM on TSMC 22ULL with an NPU for edge AI. Infineon PSoC Edge uses RRAM, ST STM32V8 uses ePCM, SEMIFIVE/ICY Tech taped out an edge-AI SoC on Samsung 8nm eMRAM, and Everspin's UNISYST sells standalone unified code+data MRAM. The only differentiator left is 16-64MB on-die (~15-60 mm2 of array, ~$1.3-5.2 of silicon at the device model's $82.9/GB). That is a niche BOM/standby-power axis against ~$10.5 of 512MB LPDDR4X now and ~$4 in a glut.

verdicts.reason: Pure software (TRL 9, T0), and the EOL wave is evidenced (Renesas serial EEPROM last-time ship 2026-10-31; DDR3/DDR4 exits), so no kill rule is clearly violated. A 2026-11 search found no vendor cross-reference tool for MRAM/F-RAM migrations, only training modules and 'drop-in replacement' marketing, so a narrow gap exists. But half the pitch is false: no emerging NVM replaces DDR3/DDR4. Everspin's largest part is a 1Gb ST-DDR4 die, not JEDEC-pin-compatible, at ~$821/GB street, ~32x DDR3 4Gb spot ($3.19/Gb ≈ $25.5/GB). The product reduces to NVM-to-NVM migrations (EEPROM/NOR/NVSRAM to F-RAM/MRAM). Incumbents are stronger than the card says: Octopart/Nexar sit inside Altium, a wholly owned Renesas subsidiary since 2024-08-01 that is building component lifecycle management. The scorer should floor moat and competition and consider folding this into C-12 or C-80 as lead-gen.
